reponse:
**What broke:** On Thursday Nov 12, from 08:47 to 12:27 UTC, customer dashboards showed stale data [1]. Ingest v2.14.0 (PR ingest#412) raised the default `max_batch_bytes` from 1 MB to 10 MB; with the workers' 512 MiB memory limit, the pods ran out of memory on the first large batch and crash-looped [1]. The change was rolled out to all pods at once, and there was no consumer-lag alert, so the first signal was a Sentry OOM alert 27 minutes after the deploy [1]. Rollback to v2.13.3 took 13 minutes once the cause was found; lag fully drained at 12:27 [1].

**Customer data:** Nothing was lost. Events kept arriving in Kafka and were processed late; reconciliation on Nov 13 showed per-workspace event counts matched Kafka offsets for 08:00–13:00 UTC [1][4]. The customer-facing incident report confirms all events were received and processed late, none lost [3]. Impact was delayed dashboards across all workspaces, with four customers contacting support [1].

**Changes we're making:**
- Alert/page on-call when ingest consumer lag exceeds 5 minutes (KES-431, due Nov 20); the rule is already routed to on-call but is still being tuned because 5 minutes also fires during nightly backfills [1][13].
- Ingest config changes go to a small canary pool first (KES-432, due Nov 27) [1][3].
- Raise worker memory limit to 1 Gi and add a load test on batch sizes (KES-433, due Nov 27) [1][3].
- Already merged in ingest#419: default `max_batch_bytes` reverted to 1 MB, plus a batcher guard that refuses batches above 25% of the container memory limit and logs a warning; the bulk-import path keeps 10 MB explicitly on its own 2 Gi pool [10].

One customer-facing loose end: Orbitly is requesting an SLA service credit under section 7 of its custom 2024 MSA, and Sam Ortiz is checking the terms with finance [3].
